title: Measuring verifier quality: precision, recall and abstention per slice, with intervals
purpose: Score the labelled gold sets with every rule-based verifier, old and new, and compute precision, recall and abstention per slice with 95% intervals. The gold sets mix correct, wrong, adversarial, equivalent-form and cosmetic completions whose correctness is known by construction.

steps.display: vq.py job q-math-final-answer-1-0-0 -- quality --verifier math-final-answer@1.0.0 --gold math_gold.jsonl
vq.py job q-math-final-answer-2-0-0 -- quality --verifier math-final-answer@2.0.0 --gold math_gold.jsonl
vq.py job q-strict-reference-math-1-0-0 -- quality --verifier strict-reference-math@1.0.0 --gold math_gold.jsonl
vq.py job q-eval-math-1-0-0 -- quality --verifier eval-math@1.0.0 --gold math_gold.jsonl
vq.py job q-code-tests-1-0-0 -- quality --verifier code-tests@1.0.0 --gold code_gold.jsonl
vq.py job q-code-tests-2-0-0 -- quality --verifier code-tests@2.0.0 --gold code_gold.jsonl
vq.py job q-strict-reference-code-1-0-0 -- quality --verifier strict-reference-code@1.0.0 --gold code_gold.jsonl
aws s3 cp s3://<bucket>/evals/quality/<each>.json -   # per slice

checks.description: the old math verifier accepts wrong answers: precision on the adversarial slice is near zero
checks.because: It passes if ANY box is right, or the last number is right when there is no box: multiple answers and number soup pass.

checks.description: the strict math verifier accepts nothing wrong, and the lower end of its 95% interval is above 0.95
checks.because: Exactly one box, no hedge, SymPy equality; anything outside the narrow language abstains.

checks.description: strictness costs recall: correct answers without a box are rejected, and boxed units abstain
checks.because: The design accepts false negatives for fewer false positives, and states the contract in the prompt.

checks.description: equivalent forms (0.5, 1/2, 2/4, \frac{1}{2}) are all accepted by the strict verifier
checks.because: Equality is symbolic, not string matching.

checks.description: the old code verifier passes printed-then-crashed, early-exit and hard-coded programs; the new one passes none and accepts every harmless rewrite
checks.because: code-tests@1 compares printed output for the visible examples only; code-tests@2 runs hidden tests in new processes and checks the exit code.
